definitions.explanation: Responding argumentatively or defiantly to someone of higher status such as a parent, teacher, or boss. Viewed negatively in Japanese culture as disrespectful behavior.

examples.japanese: {子供|こども}が{親|おや}に{口|くち}ごたえをした。
examples.english: The child talked back to his parents.

examples.japanese: {先生|せんせい}に{口|くち}ごたえばかりしていたら、{怒|おこ}られるのは{当然|とうぜん}だ。
examples.english: If you keep talking back to the teacher, of course you'll get scolded.

notes:
COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
・{口|くち}ごたえをする (talk back)
・{口|くち}ごたえするな (don't talk back)
・{親|おや}に{口|くち}ごたえする (talk back to one's parents)

USAGE NOTES:
Always carries a negative connotation — it implies insubordination or rudeness from someone who should show deference. The command {口|くち}ごたえするな is a classic phrase heard from parents and authority figures. Can be written as {口答|くちごた}え with kanji, though the hiragana form ごたえ is more common. Not to be confused with {歯|は}ごたえ (bite, texture of food) or {手|て}ごたえ (response, feedback).
